title: field-add-spec
description: INPUT of `dmtool -m <model> field add <spec.json>` — a field to add, with its full per-kind config and creation-time field metadata. The simpler `field add --group --name (--kind|--typedef)` flags cover a bare field; this spec covers everything the typed builders express. Post-creation field semantics use the narrower `schema field modify`; labels, descriptions, and annotations use `dmtool meta <ref>` (G45). `additionalProperties:false` is enforced: an undeclared/typo'd key is rejected with RK_UNKNOWN_ARG, not silently ignored. Validated against the real kernel before writing.

group.description: the parent group's ABSOLUTE name-path, e.g. /Order (must exist)

name.description: the new field's name (unique within its group)

kind.description: STRING | NUMBER | DATE | TIME | DATETIME | DATERANGE | DATEFRAGMENT | BOOLEAN | CONFIRM | ENUM | CUSTOM (omit when `typedef` is given)

typedef.description: type the field by an existing type-definition id (wins over `kind`)

required.description: true (always required) | false (optional, default) | "ifParentPresent" (required only if the parent group is filled)

label.description: per-locale display label, { "<locale>": "<text>" }; once set, must cover every declared locale

global.description: the kernel `global` flag (relevant to partial validation)

transient.description: the kernel `transient` flag (present at runtime, not persisted)

internalDescription.description: per-locale INTERNAL description — maintenance/technical notes shown read-only to *Form modelers*, never surfaced to end users; { "<locale>": "<text>" }

externalDescription.description: per-locale EXTERNAL description — the end-user-facing hint shown beside the field in the form UI; { "<locale>": "<text>" }

requiredMessages.description: per-locale custom error text shown when this REQUIRED field is left empty, { "<locale>": "<text>" } — the 'Use Default Error Messages' deselected case; needs `required` true/"ifParentPresent", must cover every declared locale, omit to use the kernel default

minLength.description: minimum character length. seeAlso: the Length operator — the rule-level way to bound length (`operators Length`)

pattern.description: anchored Java Pattern; REQUIRES patternMessage (a pattern and its error message must be set together — patternMessages alone is rejected). Authoring first requires Java syntax, then the kernel 30.8.x restrictions: the finite A12K-30 blacklist (possessive quantifiers, (?<… / (?>…), \A \G \Z \z \a \e \p \Q \E — lowercase \p only, uppercase \P is admitted — and nested unescaped [), read on the pattern SOURCE TEXT so an escaped metacharacter before a quantifier (a\*+) is refused too. Passing them does not prove JavaScript portability. seeAlso: the PatternViolated/PatternMatched operators — the rule-level alternative (`operators PatternViolated`)

patternMessage.description: the error text shown when the pattern fails; REQUIRED whenever `pattern` is set (the base message, applied to every declared locale unless patternMessages overrides a locale). A `pattern` without it is rejected: 'a pattern and its error message must be set together'

patternMessages.description: OPTIONAL per-locale override ON TOP of patternMessage, { "<locale>": "<text>" }; wins over patternMessage for that locale (patternMessage stays the required base/fallback for the rest) — the string sibling of an enum's per-locale invalid-value text, so a bilingual model can localize the pattern error. It does NOT stand alone: supply patternMessage too, or the field is rejected

noValueValidation.description: skip the kernel's per-value validation (each stored value) (for base64 blobs / attachment content etc.); the kernel REQUIRES lineBreaks alongside it (MVK_STRING_TYPE_NO_VAL_AND_NO_LINE_BREAK), so set lineBreaks:true too or the field is rejected. A raw-type field's VALUE is then unusable in rules/computations — presence checks only; the sole value-shaped exception, a whole-condition Length(f) > c, is a max-length declaration the kernel eliminates (see `dmtool diagnostics MVK_INVALID_RAW_TYPE`). Read back via `field read` under string.noValueValidation

suggestions.description: per-locale hint list, { "<locale>": ["…"] }; validated against the field's own pattern

maxFractionalDigits.description: the decimal scale; together they bound the fraction-digit range

min.description: minimum value (decimal as a string). seeAlso: the LessThan/GreaterThan comparison operators — rule-level bounds

minLength.description: minimum character length of the rendered stored-number text; sign and decimal separator count

maxLength.description: maximum character length of the rendered stored-number text; this is the Date/Time component declaration gate, not maxIntegerDigits

maxIntegerDigits.description: maximum digits before the decimal separator; sign and fractional digits do not count

positivesOnly.description: forbid a SIGN (the kernel's NumberType.positivesOnly; default false, so every field is signed unless you set this). MEASURED: a minus makes the value the formal error zahlMitVorzeichen, a ZERO magnitude included — where a signed field instead reports zahlNullEnthaeltVorzeichen, so the two classes are DISJOINT rather than ordered. It also flips the empty-operand FILL polarity: an unsigned empty number can be filled bigger but never smaller. A NEGATIVE min beside it is kernel-VALID (measured) and the value refusal still fires. seeAlso: min — a non-negative min bounds the VALUE without changing the sign polarity.

values.description: ≥1 { value, labels? } — stored value + optional per-locale labels. seeAlso: FieldValueIncludedInValueList / FieldValueNotIncludedInValueList — the rule-level way to (dis)allow a value set

categories.description: named classifications; each has values[] aligned 1:1 with the enum values. seeAlso: the EnumCategory operator (`operators EnumCategory`) — reads a value's category in a rule

description.description: optional editor-level note for the category (the kernel core ignores it; preserved for the editor's Category table)

values.description: values aligned 1:1 with the enum values

sValue.description: the stored-token S-value — the model-owned INDEX default: when this enum is a repeatable group's index field, full validation transiently supplies this token for a nonmandatory index that is absent/present-empty on the parent's only row (partial validation instead silently suppresses that cell). Must name one of the declared values (checked at authoring — the kernel stages it into evaluation unvalidated)

invalidValueMessage.description: error text for an out-of-domain value — one text expanded across ALL declared locales (the shorthand)

errorMessages.description: per-locale invalid-value error text, { "<locale>": "<text>" } — wins over invalidValueMessage; must cover every declared locale (omit both to use the kernel default)

format.description: a CASE-SENSITIVE Java pattern from a fixed allowed WHITELIST, not a compositional rule. The gate reads the STRING and never the field's KIND, so the vocabulary is shared across DATE/TIME/DATETIME. THIRTEEN patterns are admitted in total, derived from the kernel in docs/TEMPORAL-FORMAT-VOCABULARY.md (cite that file rather than re-listing): the complete dates yyyy-MM-dd, dd.MM.yyyy and yyyyMMdd; the component-omitting yyyy, yyyy-MM, yyyyMM, MM, MM-dd, MMdd, ddMM and dd.MM.; the clock HH:mm:ss; and the instant yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss — every one of them admitted on any of the three kinds, and meaning what its string says. Refused: MM.yyyy, MM-yyyy, yyyy/MM and dd.MM — so the SEPARATOR discriminates between formats with the same components (yyyy-MM is admitted, yyyy/MM is not; MMdd and ddMM are admitted while dd.MM is not, and a TRAILING separator counts too: dd.MM. with the closing dot IS admitted where dd.MM is not), and component order alone does not explain the set either. Note dd.MM is refused here yet is a legal DATERANGE format with -. Case is significant and is NOT merely lowercase: MM means months where mm means minutes, so yyyy-mm-dd is a different pattern rather than a miscased one. MEASURED: no all-lowercase or all-uppercase spelling of any admitted format is accepted, the editor's UPPERCASE display labels included. Copy a spelling from the vocabulary rather than recasing one. The A12 editor's UPPERCASE labels (YYYY-MM-DD) are display labels, NOT valid format values. Case is significant and is NOT merely lowercase: MM means months where mm means minutes, so yyyy-mm-dd is a different pattern rather than a miscased one. MEASURED: no all-lowercase or all-uppercase spelling of any admitted format is accepted, the editor's UPPERCASE display labels included. Copy a spelling from the vocabulary rather than recasing one. Default yyyy-MM-dd.

precision.description: FULL (default) | DAY_OPTIONAL | MONTH_OPTIONAL | YEAR_OPTIONAL; every precision still admits fully known dates

rejectBefore1900.description: when true, enable A12 DateType.youngerThan1900Check: stored and computed dates before 1900-01-01 are invalid; default false. MEASURED: this REQUIRES the declared format to carry a YEAR — the year-free HH:mm:ss, MM, MM-dd, MMdd, ddMM and dd.MM. are refused MVK_ADDITIONAL_CHECK_INVALID (an INCOMPLETE format is not the trigger: yyyy and yyyy-MM carry no day and are accepted).

format.description: a Java pattern from the shared temporal WHITELIST — the gate reads the string, not the kind. HH:mm (no seconds) is rejected; a date pattern such as yyyy-MM-dd is admitted on a TIME field, so the default is a convention rather than a restriction. Default HH:mm:ss.
a CASE-SENSITIVE Java date+time pattern; verify the exact accepted form with a `field add --dry-run`.

a CASE-SENSITIVE Java date pattern for both endpoints, from a fixed allowed set (independent of locale/conditionLanguage). It is the PAIR (format, separator) that is allowlisted, never the format alone — see `separator` for the eight admitted pairs. The seven formats that appear in one are dd.MM.yyyy, yyyy-MM-dd, yyyy, yyyy-MM, MM, MM-dd, dd.MM; note yyyyMM is a legal DATE format but not a legal DATERANGE one, and dd.MM is the reverse. The editor's UPPERCASE preset labels (YYYY-MM-DD, MM/MM, …) are display labels, NOT valid format values. Case is significant and is NOT merely lowercase: MM means months where mm means minutes, so yyyy-mm-dd is a different pattern rather than a miscased one. MEASURED: no all-lowercase or all-uppercase spelling of any admitted format is accepted, the editor's UPPERCASE display labels included. Copy a spelling from the vocabulary rather than recasing one.

separator.description: the range separator PAIRED with the format; the PAIR is allowlisted, and exactly eight are admitted: - for dd.MM.yyyy and dd.MM, / for yyyy-MM-dd, yyyy, yyyy-MM, MM, MM-dd, and the empty separator for MM (which halves the stored value). Everything else is rejected ('The date range format is invalid'): every separator swap, the whole '.' column, a spaced ' - ', and yyyyMM with any separator.

interpretationOfYear.description: which endpoint of a WRAPPING yearless range keeps the base year — it matters only for a range whose two endpoints do not share a year (e.g. 01.11-31.01 on a dd.MM range), which without it reads as start-after-end and is reported invalid. The direction is the REVERSE of what the names suggest: the value names the endpoint the base year LABELS and the opposite one moves, so FROM keeps the start at the base year and rolls the END forward a year, while TO keeps the end and rolls the START back. The default is STANDARD (both endpoints take the base year) and it has NO spelling — express it by OMITTING this key; the tool API's STANDARD, PREVIOUS and SUBSEQUENT tokens are all refused by the kernel. Effective only when the model declares a base year (set it with `config modify`).

rejectBefore1900.description: when true, enable A12 DateRangeType.youngerThan1900Check: a range whose START date is before 1900-01-01 is invalid (datumBereichDatumFalsch; end >= start covers the other endpoint); default false. MEASURED and UNLIKE the date/dateFragment key: NO year co-requirement — every admitted (format, separator) pair takes it, the year-free ones included, and on a year-free pair the check reads the model's BASE YEAR completion. One exception: the pure MM pair, where the kernel appends no year at all, so neither this check nor the always-on 1583-10-16 floor ever fires on it.

trueValue.description: A12 BooleanType.notInDCustomTrueValue / notInDCustomFalseValue: the text this model stores for true and for false where they are not A12's defaults. Independent — set either alone; omitting both writes no config block at all.

falseValue.description: A12 BooleanType.notInDCustomTrueValue / notInDCustomFalseValue: the text this model stores for true and for false where they are not A12's defaults. Independent — set either alone; omitting both writes no config block at all.

trueValue.description: A12 ConfirmType.notInDCustomTrueValue / notInDCustomFalseValue: the text this model stores for true and for false where they are not A12's defaults. Independent — set either alone; omitting both writes no config block at all.

falseValue.description: A12 ConfirmType.notInDCustomTrueValue / notInDCustomFalseValue: the text this model stores for true and for false where they are not A12's defaults. Independent — set either alone; omitting both writes no config block at all.

rejectBefore1900.description: when true, enable A12 DateFragmentType.youngerThan1900Check: values resolving before 1900-01-01 are invalid (datumFalsch); default false. MEASURED: like the date key and UNLIKE dateRange, this REQUIRES the declared format to carry a YEAR — the year-free HH:mm:ss, MM, MM-dd, MMdd, ddMM and dd.MM. are refused MVK_ADDITIONAL_CHECK_INVALID, while dd.MM.yyyy, yyyy, yyyy-MM, yyyy-MM-dd, yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss, yyyyMM and yyyyMMdd accept it.

format.description: a CASE-SENSITIVE Java partial-date pattern (a date that isn't a full calendar date). MEASURED: the fragment kind admits the SAME TWELVE patterns as DATE/TIME/DATETIME — see docs/TEMPORAL-FORMAT-VOCABULARY.md, which probes it as its own domain rather than inheriting the shared answer. MM, yyyy, yyyy-MM and MM-dd are the conventional fragment declarations, not the limit. The A12 editor's UPPERCASE labels (YYYY, YYYY-MM) are display labels, NOT valid format values. Case is significant and is NOT merely lowercase: MM means months where mm means minutes, so yyyy-mm-dd is a different pattern rather than a miscased one. MEASURED: no all-lowercase or all-uppercase spelling of any admitted format is accepted, the editor's UPPERCASE display labels included. Copy a spelling from the vocabulary rather than recasing one.
